goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook returns raw verbatim for cook_methods[:raw_html] in app/models/post.rb:131, so feed/embed-imported HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized, enabling stored XSS via PollFeed → TopicEmbed.import with no sanitize/whitelist step

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is typically where Discourse sanitizes/filters HTML). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` where `contents` comes from untrusted sources. In particular, `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` pulls `i.content` from an external RSS/ATOM feed, only does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and then calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)` without any sanitization/whitelisting. `absolutize_urls` rewrites relative links but does not remove scripts/event handlers. The embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, so any injected HTML/JS would execute. This is a verifiable stored XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 edits an already-shipped migration to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which drops the existing table and its data if re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which would delete any existing `top_topics` data if this migration is ever executed against a DB that already has that table (e.g., rerun/redo, certain reset flows). This behavior is directly implied by the `force: true` option.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:16-31 does check-then-create on embed_url with a unique index, so concurrent imports raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique after creating a duplicate topic/post

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to create a post/topic and then `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. There is a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` added in the migration. Under concurrent imports of the same URL, both callers can observe `embed.blank?` and race to `create!`, causing the second transaction to raise an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`/unique constraint violation. The method does not rescue this, and callers like Jobs::PollFeed / TopicRetriever also don’t handle it, so the race can crash the job/request. The claim that a duplicate topic/post will be left behind is not strictly guaranteed because the create happens inside a DB transaction, but the unhandled race/exception is real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-29 uses setnx followed by a separate expire non-atomically, so a crash between calls leaves the key without a TTL and throttles that embed_url forever

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb retrieved_recently? does `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then in a separate call `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two operations are not atomic. If the process crashes or loses the Redis connection after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without a TTL, and subsequent calls will see `setnx` return false and treat it as “retrieved recently” forever for that embed_url (until the key is manually deleted). This is a real correctness/availability bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:12 mutates the caller's string in place with `contents << ...`, corrupting reused content and raising on frozen strings

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the `contents` argument in-place, mutating the caller-provided String. This is verifiable from the diff: `<<` modifies the receiver. That can be a correctness defect because (a) callers that reuse the same string instance will see it unexpectedly modified, and (b) if a frozen string is ever passed (common with frozen string literals / `# frozen_string_literal: true` or other freezing), this will raise `FrozenError` at runtime. The method does not document or defensively copy `contents`, so the side effect is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:41-46 asserts TopicRetriever.new/retrieve are called, but the controller enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic, so the test exercises nothing real

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders 'loading'. It never instantiates `TopicRetriever` directly. However, spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb (the "tells the topic retriever to work" example) sets `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)...` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, which cannot be satisfied by the controller code as written. The job (Jobs::RetrieveTopic) is what uses TopicRetriever, but that is not invoked synchronously here. So the spec is asserting the wrong behavior and would fail / not test the real code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:19 defines feed_key (feed-modified: cache key) but never uses it, so the feed is refetched and all items reimported hourly with no conditional GET

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is indeed defined and never referenced anywhere in this diff, so it is dead/unused code. However, the finding’s causal claim that this results in “all items reimported hourly” is not strictly supported: the job is intentionally scheduled `hourly`, and each item is passed through `TopicEmbed.import`, which deduplicates by `embed_url` and only revises when `content_sha1` changes. There is also no evidence in the diff that `feed_key` was intended for conditional GET or that its absence is a correctness bug (it’s more an optimization/cleanup opportunity).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:44 calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside a per-URL retrieval job, blocking one embed request on fetching and importing an entire feed

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` unconditionally does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs synchronous network I/O (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and iterates/imports *all* feed items. This happens in the per-URL retrieval path (triggered by `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` for a single `embed_url`), so a single embed retrieval can block a Sidekiq worker on fetching/parsing/importing an entire feed, potentially redundantly and with high latency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5-11 lacks a null check on document.getElementById('discourse-comments'), so appendChild throws and breaks the host page's JS if the container is missing

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `comments` is assigned from `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and immediately used as `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no guard. If the element is absent (e.g., host page forgot to include the container or script executes before DOM is ready), `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a TypeError, breaking subsequent JS on the page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:60-71 absolutize_urls only rewrites URLs starting with /, leaving document-relative and protocol-relative URLs broken

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the code only rewrites href/src when the value `start_with?('/')`. This misses common document-relative URLs like `images/foo.png` or `../page`, which will remain relative and likely break when rendered under the Discourse domain (contradicting the method comment: "Convert any relative URLs to absolute"). Additionally, protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x` also start with `/` and will be incorrectly rewritten to `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x` (e.g., `http://site.com/cdn.example.com/x`), which is wrong.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile:209 adds ruby-readability and simple-rss to Gemfile and Gemfile_rails4.lock without updating the primary Gemfile.lock, breaking frozen/deployment bundle install

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new gems added to Gemfile and corresponding entries added to Gemfile_rails4.lock, but it does not show whether a standard Gemfile.lock exists or is used as the “primary” lockfile in this repo. Many projects with alternate Gemfiles/locks (e.g., for Rails 4) intentionally update only the relevant lockfile. Since the presence/role of a main Gemfile.lock and whether bundler is run in frozen/deployment mode against it is not verifiable from this diff alone, the claim that this will break deployment is speculative.
